title: Example meter - stored volume
description: Illustrative derived meter, published under the reserved `example` vendor so that no deployment can mistake it for a real declaration. It exists to pin the derivation pattern every meter follows: reference the base, resolve its traits, and close the metadata surface. Nothing structural is restated - the entry shape is inherited from the base. Stored volume is the worked case deliberately: consumption of a stored volume is naturally a level, and no fold this gear offers integrates a level series, so the emitter pre-integrates into accrued `byte-hours` and the meter declares `SUM`. A meter declaring the same series in `bytes` would be a different, and wrong, declaration. Meters are leaves - `x-gts-final` forbids a sub-type, matching the base's rule of exactly one derivation segment.

metadata.description: Closed metadata surface for this meter. Declared equals queryable: both properties are groupable and equality-filterable on the raw and aggregate read paths, and an entry carrying any other key is rejected before persistence. The base admits any key with a string value; this subschema forbids undeclared keys, and the two intersect to exactly the properties below.

region.description: Placement region of the stored volume.

storage_class.description: Durability or performance tier the volume was billed at.
